He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]], and [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State Vikings]]. ==Early career== Born in [[Almere]], Enaruna started playing junior basketball with [[Almere Pioneers]].{{cite news|title=Tristan Enaruna (18) uit Almere komt steeds dichter bij zijn droom: de NBA|url=https://www.parool.nl/sport/tristan-enaruna-18-uit-almere-komt-steeds-dichter-bij-zijn-droom-de-nba~be13e58a/|publisher=Parool.nl|date=22 February 2020|access-date=9 October 2024}} He later played for the youth academy of [[Apollo Amsterdam]]. In the [[2017–18 DBL season|2017–18 season]], Enaruna made his debut with [[Apollo Amsterdam]] in the professional [[Dutch Basketball League]] (DBL) at age 16. He earned a spot on the roster alongside his brother Iyen. On July 10, 2017, Enaruna played his first professional game, playing 7 minutes in a 82–80 win over [[Rotterdam Basketbal|Rotterdam]]. Over the course of the season, he participated in three games, averaging 12 minutes and 2.7 points per game.{{cite web|title=Tristan Enaruna Player Profile, BC Apollo Amsterdam, International Stats, Events Stats, Game Logs, Awards - RealGM|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tristan-Enaruna/Summary/118675|website=RealGM.com|access-date=29 April 2019}} In the 2018–19 season, Enaruna played with [[Wasatch Academy]] in the United States. ==College career== In May 2019, Enaruna committed to play collegiately for [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web|title=What to expect from KU basketball's newest player, Tristan Enaruna|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article230170734.html|website=KansasCity.com|access-date=13 May 2019}} On 19 April 2021, Enaruna transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web|first1=Matthew|last1=Bain|first2=Travis|last2=Hines|title=Kansas transfer Tristan Enaruna pledges to Iowa State men's basketball|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2021/04/19/iowa-state-basketball-kansas-transfer-tristan-enaruna-pledges-tj-otzelberger/7287031002/|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=19 April 2021|access-date=20 April 2021}} He scored a career-high 23 points on January 1, 2022, in a 77-72 loss to [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]].{{cite news|title=Top-ranked Baylor holds on to beat No. 8 Iowa State 77-72|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401368352|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=1 January 2022|access-date=2 January 2022}} In April 2022, Enaruna transferred to [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]].{{cite news|first=Gary|last=Bedore|title=Former KU, Iowa State men’s basketball player Tristan Enaruna makes transfer decision|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article260615772.html|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=April 20, 2022|access-date=March 9, 2024}} He averaged 15.1 points and 6.6 rebounds per game and was named to the First Team All-[[Horizon League]].{{cite news|first=Tyler|last=Carey|title=Cleveland State men's basketball star Tristan Enaruna named 1st-team All-Horizon League
